absent: Numeric bounds for interrupt-chip pin and chip counts and detailed MSI flag semantics beyond field copying.
Internal behavior of SPI injection, ITS presence and initialization tests, MSI-to-ITS resolution, LPI resolution and lookup, queueing, reference handling, and locked guest access helpers.
Version-zero ITS table save, restore and commit procedures and guest collection, device and translation entry encodings.
Host hardware-backed interrupt and virtual-LPI mapping operations and the numeric meanings of ITS command error codes.
Full layouts of ITS device, collection, translation entry, distributor and interrupt objects beyond fields touched here.
Register encodings for TYPER, BASER, IIDR, PROPBASER and PENDBASER beyond the accessors and fields shown.
Command-queue processing order and lifecycle rules for device and collection objects.

findings.text: Routing setup supports interrupt-chip and message kinds. Chip kind binds the SPI path and records chip and pin subject to bounds checks; message kind binds the message path and records address halves, payload, flags and device identity. Unknown kinds or out-of-range chip or pin selections are rejected with an invalid-input outcome.

Message delivery through a routing entry requires an ITS-capable virtual machine and an asserted level, otherwise reporting device-missing or level-rejected outcomes. On acceptance the stored routing fields are transferred into a transient message object that is handed to the ITS injector.

Top-level MSI injection prefers a cached translation when one exists and otherwise resolves the owning ITS from the message and triggers under that ITS lock. Transport failures propagate as negative outcomes while mapping-related results are normalized so positive means delivered and zero means guest-masked.

Triggering from device and event identities resolves a local interrupt object. Hardware-backed interrupts are marked pending through the host controller; software interrupts are marked pending under their own lock and queued. Resolution failures propagate.

Cached injection derives a doorbell address from the two message address halves, rejects out-of-range device or event identities, locates the ITS by doorbell, and looks up the cached interrupt with reference acquisition under read-side protection. A hit marks pending under lock, queues and releases the reference; a miss reports a retryable condition.

Atomic-context injection never blocks. Deasserted levels are rejected as retryable. Messages use only the cached path when an ITS exists; chip SPIs inject directly when the distributor is initialized. All other cases report retryable.

LPI creation is idempotent by identifier. A live existing object is returned with its reference retained. Otherwise a new object starts edge-triggered, grouped and singly referenced toward the requesting CPU, is inserted under distributor table lock with concurrent-winner reuse and dead-entry eviction, then is hydrated from guest configuration and pending state with failure dropping the reference.

Configuration refresh reads one guest property byte addressed from the property base by identifier offset. Under interrupt lock it installs priority and enable state when no CPU filter is given or the filter matches the target, queueing software interrupts immediately; hardware-backed state is delegated to the host updater with an invalidation hint.

Single-LPI pending synchronization loads the guest pending bit for the current target CPU, installs it into the latch under lock with retry if affinity moved during the load, queues the interrupt, and clears the consumed guest bit when set. Interrupts without a target require no work.

Bulk pending synchronization for one CPU scans all distributor LPIs, reusing the last-read guest pending byte for consecutive identifiers sharing that byte, and for each located interrupt installs the relevant bit under lock only when that CPU is the current target before queueing and releasing.

ITS table ABI is described by three entry sizes plus save, restore and commit operations. The known table holds one revision with uniform eight-byte entries and version-zero handlers. The active revision index is stored per ITS, retrieved by lookup, and changed by assignment followed by commit.

Local interrupts start at identifier 8192. Device and event identifier spaces each span sixteen bits with maxima one below two to the sixteenth. Direct-table offset caps are one below two to the fourteenth for devices and one below two to the sixteenth for events.
Revision-zero ITS table entries are eight bytes for collection, device and translation tables, and the maximum entry size equals eight. The ABI revision count equals the length of the revision table.
A guest LPI property byte carries an enable indication in its lowest bit and a priority value in its upper six bits.

ITS command words encode nine parameters at fixed word positions and widths: command selector, device identity, size bias, event identity, physical identity, collection identity, translation-table address, target address and valid bit, decoded from little-endian words with masking.

ITS identity MMIO reports a type value combining physical-interrupt support with encoded device-bit, identifier-bit and entry-size fields, a revision value combining active ABI revision with fixed product and implementer identities, and fixed part, architecture and software-page values at defined offsets with zero elsewhere. Privileged revision selection validates against the known revision count before installing and committing.
Register windowing returns the requested byte slice of a sixty-four-bit value selected by byte offset and length.

Guest ITS table transfers size the access from the active ABI revision for the table kind and require agreement between that size and the caller buffer, with compile-time enforcement for the single-revision build and run-time rejection otherwise, before performing locked guest read or write.
Guest table stores bracket the underlying locked write with a distributor flag marking a table update as in progress.

Affinity reassignment optionally validates an expected previous CPU, updates the target under interrupt lock, and for hardware-backed interrupts transfers host association with handover of virtual-CPU counts and host remap. Per-entry updates apply only when the entry collection is mapped; collection-wide updates visit every device entry of the ITS and filter to the named collection.

Collection lookup scans the ITS collection list for a matching identifier and returns null when absent. The property-base implied LPI maximum derives from its low five bits plus one, capped by the architectural ITS identifier width.

Per-ITS translation-cache invalidation erases every cached entry and drops the cache-held reference for each erased interrupt. Global invalidation walks the virtual-machine device list under read-side protection, selects ITS devices by operations identity, and applies per-ITS invalidation.

Discard succeeds only for a known device-event entry whose collection is mapped, invalidating translations, detaching and releasing the entry including host unmap and clearing of the hardware mark, and clearing the guest translation entry; otherwise it reports unmapped-interrupt. Move succeeds only for a known entry with mapped source and mapped destination collections, rebinding the collection, invalidating translations and moving affinity; otherwise it reports unmapped-interrupt or unmapped-collection.

BASER identifier validation accepts only device and collection table types with type-specific bounds and rejects unknown types. Flat tables are checked for capacity with a directly derived address; indirect tables are checked for first-level capacity, require the first-level valid bit after a locked guest load, then derive the second-level address by masking and offsetting. Both paths require guest-visible memory and optionally return the entry address.

Slow-path MSI triggering serializes on the owning ITS lock. Per-interrupt mutable state including pending latch, target, priority and enable is protected by that interrupt lock held across update plus queueing. Distributor LPI insertion and eviction serialize on the LPI table lock.

Translation-cache lookup and global device-list walks run under read-side critical sections with reference acquisition for retained objects. Guest frame visibility checks run under a scoped read lock. Scoped guards provide the same interrupt-lock exclusion for affinity and teardown paths.

Guest table reads and writes can fail and failures propagate, including property, pending, indirect-level and translation entries. Affinity may change during pending loads so the target must be rechecked under lock. Concurrent LPI creation may race so insertion must detect a live winner. Stale cached translations must be invalidated on discard, move and remap. Hardware-backed teardown must clear the hardware mark under lock before releasing.
